assessment: This is a one-card sideboard: Red Mana and Storm Counter are Secret Lair table accessories with type_line "Card" and no rules text, so they are bookkeeping aids, not swap candidates. The one real card, Sazacap's Brew, is not a Zada card and the deck's published artifacts currently say otherwise. Zada copies an instant or sorcery only when it "targets only Zada"; Sazacap's Brew's first target is a player ("Target player draws two cards"), and even with the gift promised it targets a player plus a creature — so it never targets only Zada, Zada never triggers on it, and it also never triggers Frontline Heroism, which wants a spell targeting only a single creature you control. Strip the copy fantasy away and what is left is a two-mana instant that discards a card as an additional cost to draw two: card-neutral selection plus one storm count, which is a fine card in the abstract and the worst cantrip in this specific 99, where Crimson Wisps and Expedite cost {R} and turn every body into a card (verified stack 001). It earns a slot only in a narrow, nameable spot, and its role tag buff:pump — read off the conditional +2/+0 rider — is the taxonomy misdescribing a draw spell.

swaps.role: draw:burst (instant-speed selection) — NOT buff:pump; the taxonomy tagged it off the conditional +2/+0 rider
swaps.when: Pre-game or between games against a creature-light pod — spellslinger, enchantress, superfriends, a stax deck whose only bodies are mana rocks — where Spreading Insurrection has nothing worth stealing, AND no opponent is on graveyard hate (Rest in Peace, Soulless Jailer, Bojuka Bog). Do not make this swap against a creature pod, and do not make it at all if the table can exile your graveyard.
swaps.why: Spreading Insurrection is a five-mana sorcery that needs both a high storm count and an opposing creature worth stealing; against a pod with no attackers it is a dead card in a deck whose curve already tops out at fifteen 1-drops, while Sazacap's Brew is castable on turn 2 at instant speed, and its mandatory discard is the deck's cheapest way to bin Past in Flames, Faithless Looting, Wild Ride or Impulsive Pilferer, all of which pay you back from the graveyard via flashback, harmonize or encore.

citations.quote: mulligan and sideboard decisions are largely virtual-advantage decisions
cut the ceiling card before the median one
Keep the near-misses as a sideboard and swap them in between games.

opens_lines.why_plausible: Sazacap's Brew's discard is an additional cost paid on cast, before the draw-two resolves, so it is a discard outlet rather than a loot. Past in Flames has flashback {4}{R} and Faithless Looting has flashback {2}{R}; Wild Ride has harmonize {4}{R} and Impulsive Pilferer has encore {3}{R}. Binning one of those four on turn 2 converts the cost into deferred value and sets up the Past in Flames ritual rebuild the strategic frame already lists as a candidate line. What is unresolved is the sequencing and the mana: whether the deck can profitably pay the discard early and still reach the flashback cost on the storm turn, and whether Storm-Kiln Artist's magecraft Treasure from the Brew cast changes that arithmetic.

long_term_defaults.why: It is dominated in the 99 by cards already in the list. Witch's Mark is the same cost ({1}{R}), the same discard-one-draw-two effect, and its discard is optional rather than a cost you cannot pay with an empty hand — and because its only target is "up to one target creature you control", pointing it at Zada makes it a spell that targets only Zada, which the Brew can never be. Crimson Wisps and Expedite do the cantrip job for {R} and copy off Zada per body (verified stack 001). Sazacap's Brew also has no EDHREC rank, so there is no popularity signal to argue from, and its gift rider hands an opponent a tapped 1/1 blue Fish — one more blocker in front of a deck that wins by attacking wide with 1/1 Goblins, which is a real cost, not a freeroll.

gaps: CONTRADICTION TO RESOLVE, NOT SILENTLY: strategic_frame.json engines[0] lists "Sazacap's Brew" inside the Zada cantrip set ("with cantrips (Crimson Wisps, Expedite, Ancestors' Aid, Renegade Tactics, Wild Ride, Witch's Mark, Sazacap's Brew, Great Train Heist) each body becomes a card"). That is wrong on oracle text: the Brew targets a player, so Zada never triggers. It should be removed from that list. Great Train Heist should also be checked — its Spree modes target an opponent, not a creature.

PRIOR CLAIM EVALUATED AND REJECTED: manual_prose.json says of Sazacap's Brew, "Test it in the Witch's Mark slot if your meta runs graveyard-light." That is the one slot it must not take — Witch's Mark is Zada-copyable and the Brew is not, so the swap trades the deck's only copyable draw-two for a non-copyable one. The prose's "draw two, discard one" also inverts the order: the discard is an additional cost paid on cast, so you discard blind before you see the two cards, and you cannot cast the Brew off an empty hand. And the graveyard condition points the wrong way — the discard is best when the graveyard is safe (flashback/harmonize/encore payback) and worst when an opponent can exile it.

Witch's Mark targeting only Zada looks like a real, unrecorded copy engine: each copy would repeat "You may discard a card. If you do, draw two cards" for a different creature. No stack artifact covers it. Needs a stack scenario before the manual claims it.

Daring Discovery says "Up to three target creatures can't block this turn" — choosing exactly one target, Zada, would appear to make it a spell targeting only Zada, copied for a Discover 4 per body. That would make it far better than its five-mana curve slot suggests, and it changes whether it is ever a cut candidate. Needs a stack scenario.

The strategy corpus has no section on discard-as-an-additional-cost or on rummage versus loot, so the claim that a mandatory pitch is worse than an optional one rests on oracle text and on strategy:card-advantage ("a draw-two is +1 net card" — netted against the discard and the Brew itself, this card is 0), not on a cited construction principle.
